Leipzig University offers an innovative and international working environment as well as an exciting range of career opportunities in research, teaching, knowledge and technology transfer, infrastructure and administration.The Institute for Geography at the Faculty of Physics and Earth System Sciences seeks to fill the above position.The PhD position is part of the project “CASCADE – Cascading impacts of climate extremes: new perspectives for interlinking Earth System Sciences in Leipzig” on compound and cascading impacts of climate extremes. CASCADE investigates how floods and droughts affect society and the environment, combining large-scale data analysis with a systems perspective on human–environment interactions.Our knowledge of the impacts of climate extremes is only as good as the data that record them. The PhD project aims to uncover biases in climate impact databases and research and to provide a more comprehensive view of flood and drought impacts at the global scale. To this end, the doctoral researcher will link and harmonise existing databases (e.g. ROUGE, Wikimpacts, EM-DAT) into a common event, impact and spatial framework, and will contribute to developing a multilingual news-based impact dataset that helps to fill gaps in existing sources.
